title: Joint probabilities and independence
caption: Reading the table in percentage points: P(X = 1) = 0.5 and P(Y = 1) = 0.6, so independence would need P(1, 1) = 0.3. The table has 0.4, so X and Y are dependent.
alt: Two overlapping circles, X = 1 and Y = 1: X only 10, both 40, Y only 20, neither 30, out of 100.
description: The cell P(1, 1) = 0.4 is the overlap of X = 1 and Y = 1.
P(1, 0) = 0.1 is X = 1 only, and P(0, 1) = 0.2 is Y = 1 only; P(0, 0) = 0.3 is neither.
The circles' totals are P(X = 1) = 0.5 and P(Y = 1) = 0.6; 0.5 × 0.6 = 0.3 is not the overlap 0.4.
